summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening shortness of breath and left lower extremity swelling, found to have an acute exacerbation of chronic diastolic heart failure. She was treated with intravenous and then oral torsemide, resulting in improved symptoms, resolution of edema, and stable kidney function. A previously suspected atrial or ventricular septal defect was ruled out by transesophageal echocardiography, which showed the signal was due to normal blood flow dynamics. Her hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia were managed with continued medications. Given her recent move and lack of home support, she was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation. She was instructed to monitor daily weights and to follow up with her outpatient providers.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
